# ADR 0009 — Two manifests: the runtime manifest (`provides`) and the version manifest (`requires`)

Status: proposed (2026-09-10). Layer: kernel (shapes), runtime (values).
Re-expresses the contract of ADR 0004 in the vocabulary of ADR 0007.

## Context

ADR 0004 gave this runtime a contract: two halves, published as data and as
JSON Schema, checked at build time. The continuation document asks for a
**runtime manifest** generated by the module and checked against the
`requires` of each document, in the same pattern as the registry manifest.
Those are the same artifact seen from two sides, and a third artifact is
implied: the manifest of a **published version** of a document, which the
handoff describes with per-section hashes (Revision 1, 3.2) and which is
where derived `requires` must be written so thin clients can check
compatibility without an engine.

The word "manifest" is already used in this repository for
`.nuxt/blueprint/manifest.json`, the agent-facing description of the
project. This ADR names the three so they stop colliding.

## Decision

### Runtime manifest — what a runtime provides

```jsonc
{
  "runtime": "blueprint-nuxt-module",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "spec": ">=0.1 <0.2",                              // kernel range implemented
  "engine": { "name": "blueprint-engine", "version": "1.0.0", "build": "sha256:…" },  // evaluatedBy (ADR 0013)
  "surfaces": ["build", "server", "client"],
  "provides": [
    { "name": "web.pages",           "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "client", "options": { "prefix": "" } },
    { "name": "web.state",           "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "client", "options": { "persistence": "localStorage" } },
    { "name": "web.router",          "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "client" },
    { "name": "ui.toast",            "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "client" },
    { "name": "http.client",         "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "client" },
    { "name": "http.endpoints",      "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "server", "options": { "mount": "/api/blueprint", "methods": ["GET","POST","PUT","PATCH","DELETE"] } },
    { "name": "storage.collections", "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "server", "options": { "backends": ["memory","fs","sqlite"], "default": "fs", "recordFields": ["id","createdAt","updatedAt"] } },
    { "name": "time.now",            "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "any" },
    { "name": "records.pinned",      "version": "1.0.0", "surface": "server" },
    { "name": "vocab.base",          "version": "0.1.0", "surface": "client", "components": ["Text", "Heading", "…"] },
    { "name": "vocab.nuxt-ui",       "version": "3.3.0+a1b2c3", "surface": "client", "components": ["UButton", "…"] },
    { "name": "vocab.app",           "version": "0.0.0+e5f6a7", "surface": "client", "components": [] }
  ],
  "materializers": [
    { "surface": "client", "target": "vue", "vocabularies": ["vocab.base", "vocab.nuxt-ui", "vocab.app"] }
  ]
}
```

Published exactly where the contract is published today: as data
(`GET /api/blueprint/contract`, `manifest.json#runtime`) and as the JSON
Schema of the sections and vocabularies it owns (`runtime.schema.json`).
The name `contract` stays on the HTTP route for now; the object is the
manifest.

Vocabulary versions carry the registry hash as build metadata, which is the
"versioned by hash" condition of the module context (section 3.4): a
`pnpm update` of Nuxt UI changes the hash, the version manifest of every
published document that used `vocab.nuxt-ui` no longer matches, and the
build says so instead of rendering wrong.

### Version manifest — what a published document requires

Generated when a document is published (today: at build, in
`.nuxt/blueprint/`; later: by the document store, ADR 0014):

```jsonc
{
  "id": "01J9HEALTHQUOTE0000000001",
  "name": "health-quote",
  "version": "9f3c…",                                    // hash of the canonical document (ADR 0013)
  "spec": "0.1",
  "sections": {                                          // hash per section, for projections and partial delivery
    "meta": "…", "resources": "…", "schemas": "…", "definitions": "…", "state": "…",
    "actions": "…", "templates": "…", "tests": "…", "runtime": "…", "collections": "…", "endpoints": "…"
  },
  "requires": { "web.pages": "^1", "web.router": "^1", "web.state": "^1", "http.client": "^1",
                "http.endpoints": "^1", "storage.collections": "^1", "time.now": "^1", "vocab.base": "^0.1" },
  "optional": { "ui.toast": "^1" },
  "options": { "storage.collections": { "storage": "sqlite" } },
  "portability": "L1",
  "pages": ["/", "/quotes/:id", "/quotes"],
  "endpoints": ["POST /quotes", "GET /quotes/:id", "GET /quotes", "POST /quotes/:id/accept", "GET /rating", "GET /stats"],
  "tests": { "definitions": 16, "scenarios": 0 },
  "from": { "blueprintId": "…", "message": "…" }
}
```

Derived entirely from the document by `refs()`; authored fields of
`content.runtime` only add to it. It is data, stable, and hashable itself.

### Project manifest — what agents read

`.nuxt/blueprint/manifest.json` keeps its role: the list of documents with
their version manifests, plus the runtime manifest, plus the component
contracts. Renamed in prose to **project manifest**; the file name stays.

### Compatibility is computed, and the answer has three values

For a version manifest against a runtime manifest:

1. spec: the document's `spec` inside the runtime's range, else **incompatible**.
2. every `requires` entry: a `provides` entry with the same name whose version
   satisfies the range, else **incompatible** (`CAPABILITY_MISSING` or
   `CAPABILITY_VERSION`).
3. every `optional` entry: same test, failure yields **degraded** with the
   list of what will be unavailable.
4. options: each option is validated by the provider (`sqlite` must be in
   `backends`), else **incompatible** (`UNKNOWN_STORAGE` today).

`validate` prints one line per document per known runtime:

```
health-quote  spec 0.1  L1 (kernel + vocab.base)
  blueprint-nuxt-module 1.0.0   compatible
  blueprint-headless    0.1.0   degraded: web.pages, web.router, web.state, http.client, ui.toast unavailable (3 pages not served; 6 endpoints served)
```

### Portability levels, for humans

| Level | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | kernel only: definitions, tests, schemas, resources | a rating engine consumed by another system |
| L1 | L0 + `vocab.base` templates | `restaurant-menu-shop`, `hello-world` |
| L2 | L1 + the minimum common runtime capabilities (to be written, ADR 0005) | `public-board`, `health-quote`, once the list exists |
| L3 | uses a runtime-specific vocabulary or option | anything with a `U*` component or a `sqlite` option |

Levels are a summary of the requirement set, never an input; they never
change what a runtime does.

## Alternatives considered

- **One manifest for everything.** The three artifacts change at different
  times (runtime release, document publish, project build) and are read by
  different readers (validator, thin client, agent). Three names cost less
  than one overloaded one.
- **Keep the two-halves contract shape and add a `capabilities` array.**
  Transitional; the halves become `surface` tags on each capability, which
  is strictly more general and no longer to write.

## Fixtures required

- Compatibility fixtures: (version manifest, runtime manifest) → verdict,
  for each of compatible, degraded, incompatible by spec, by missing
  capability, by version, by option.
- Version manifest generation: document → manifest, for the four documents
  in `content/`, hand-reviewed once.

## Consequences

- `RUNTIME_CONTRACT` in `contract.ts` gains `spec`, `engine`, `provides`
  and `materializers`; `client`/`server` remain as derived views so
  nothing that reads them breaks.
- The build check gains spec and version checks, and prints the report
  above.
- The version manifest replaces the ad-hoc fields the build writes today
  and is the input for projection (ADR 0015) and for the document store
  (ADR 0014).
